This stage builds the plan in waves of tasks. You run it in the main
session and orchestrate: executors write the code.

## Steps

1. Run `accord anchor`. When it prints `stages off for lane <L>:` naming plan, the ticket has no `plan.md` and builds as one task: follow `./build-no-plan.md` instead of steps 2 and 3. Otherwise it names the next task. If it prints `Stage: plan` (the plan is not committed as ready), or `git status --porcelain` on `plan.md` prints anything, the plan stage has not finished: follow `./plan.md` and resume there instead of building.

2. **Dispatch.** Build the tasks in `plan.md` without a line in `accord/tickets/<id>/ledger.md` in waves, as `./build-waves.md` says; each task it builds here (`Parallel: 1`), in order, one at a time: run `accord brief <id> <n> --out brief-<n>.md`, which writes the brief into the git-ignored `.accord-reports/<id>/` folder, so it is never committed, and dispatch a fresh `accord-executor` with the path its `file:` line prints, only. Never pass chat history.

3. **Record.** When it reports, run the test command its brief printed yourself; when the brief printed none, run the test files the executor reports it wrote or changed. Then run `accord task-done <id> <n>`. The executor's claim alone records nothing.
   - It refuses because a `verify:` case failed or is missing: dispatch a fresh executor with the same brief plus the reasons it printed. If it refuses that way again after that dispatch, load `accord-debug` instead of dispatching again.
   - It refuses because no test report is loaded or the `tests.report` file was written before the last commit: the `tests.affected` command does not write that file. Tell the owner; do not loop.
   - It refuses because the executor report (its brief's `Report file`) is missing, was written before HEAD's commit, or lacks its lines: run `accord brief <id> <n> --out brief-<n>.md` again, then dispatch a fresh executor with it plus the reasons.
   - It refuses because a commit carries a forbidden line or breaks `commits.message`: reword that commit yourself if you made it, doing the fix the reason names; if an executor made it, dispatch a fresh executor with the same brief plus the reasons it printed. It exits 2 and says to run `git fetch origin`: run that. Either way, run `accord task-done <id> <n>` again.
   - It writes the `@test:` tag of each scenario a `verify:` id marks with `(@ac-n)`. It refuses because a scenario already carries a different `@test:` tag: ask the owner; never an executor or `accord-debug`.
   - It writes the ledger line: copy every Ruling in the executor's report into `accord/tickets/<id>/ledger.md` under `## Rulings`, then commit the ticket together with `accord/tickets/<id>/ledger.md`, then run `accord worktree push <id>`; go on even if it fails.
   - A ticket whose recorded tasks predate the tag writer: run `accord task-done <id> <n>` again for each recorded task.

4. **Blocked.**
   - `BLOCKED` with a question that touches intent, a veto, a criterion,
     or a public interface: ask the owner.
   - `BLOCKED` on a test that seems wrong: a criterion test is the
     owner's, so ask the owner; any other test is a plan gap and goes back
     to `./plan.md`. Never edit the test yourself.
   - `BLOCKED` on an architecture change: go to step 6. `BLOCKED` after
     three failed attempts: ask the owner, with what was tried; never
     dispatch a fresh executor for more tries. A new package: ask the
     owner.
   - `BLOCKED: conflict`: ask the owner, as for a veto.
   - `BLOCKED: context`: dispatch a fresh executor with the same brief
     plus the diff and the ledger so far.
   - `NEEDS_CONTEXT`: answer, and dispatch again.

5. **Files.** A file outside the task's `files:` line must be declared
   in the report with a reason. When you accept it, record a Ruling.

6. **Change of course.** When the approved approach cannot work, stop. Write a change note under the ticket's `## Approach`: what failed, which finished tasks still hold, and the proposed new approach. Ask the owner for a new yes; on yes run `accord approve <id>`, commit the ticket and run `accord worktree push <id>`; go on even if it fails. When `accord approve` exits 1, follow `./scout.md`. Then `./plan.md`'s re-plan covers only the tasks the change touches. Never re-plan quietly.

7. **Plan changed.** When `accord task-done` says `plan.md` changed,
   never run `accord gate plan` to clear it. Show the owner the diff of
   `plan.md`. If the owner made the change, `./plan.md` reviews it
   (critic, then `accord gate plan`); otherwise restore `plan.md` with the
   owner's yes and dispatch again. Only `./plan.md` changes the plan. Never run
   `accord tests baseline` here except as `./build-no-plan.md` says, which follows `./plan-baseline.md`; otherwise only the plan stage asks the owner about it.

8. When every task has a ledger line, next: `./review.md`. When `accord anchor` names review off, follow the section `With the review stage off` of `./review-security.md`, then `./verify.md`.

## Rules

- Every agent receives the ticket verbatim, by file path, never a summary:
  the executor gets it inside its brief.
- The main session orchestrates and never edits product code.
- Anything touching intent, a veto, an acceptance criterion, or a public
  interface stops the run and asks the owner. Every other decision is a
  Ruling in `accord/tickets/<id>/ledger.md` under `## Rulings`:
  `Ruling: <what> — <why> — <cost if wrong>`.
  Read `./ask.md` before any question to the owner.
